title: Linux_AirDropBot_Botnet_Investigation_7f7
description: Investigate and respond to unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents in a network with Linux-based systems.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these issues. The network consists of several Linux-based systems, including a command-and-control server, compromised bots, and a victim system. Use the provided access credentials to log in to the systems and perform your investigation.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the sandbox in cloud using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano, Access Method: SSH. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: Access the local sandbox using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano, Access Method: SSH. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication. Enumerate running services using `systemctl list-timers` and identify beaconing behavior associated with botnet activity.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services. The suspicious service is likely named 'bot-beacon-cloudprocess.timer'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services related to network diagnostics or system health beacons.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is likely related to periodic tasks and may have a name indicating its malicious intent.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Traffic Service
levels.content: Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic. Enumerate running services using `systemctl list-timers` and distinguish malicious traffic generation services from legitimate network services.
levels.solution: Examine the network connections and look for any services that are generating excessive traffic. The service responsible for generating abnormal traffic is likely named 'bot-flood-cloudprocess.timer'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the network connections and look for any services that are generating excessive traffic.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services related to network flooding or DDoS attacks.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The service generating abnormal traffic is likely related to flooding activities and may have a name indicating its malicious intent.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. Identify persistence mechanisms (e.g., systemd, cron, scheduled task, registry) using `systemctl list-timers`.
levels.solution: Investigate the systemd timers and services to find any persistence mechanisms. The persistence mechanism is likely the 'system-update-checker.timer' service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate the systemd timers and services to find any persistence mechanisms.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services related to system updates or health checks.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The persistence mechanism is likely a timer service that runs periodically and may have a name indicating its role in maintaining the malicious activity.
